historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Fleet introduction plan (972 aircraft end-2025 to 1,104 end-2028, 4.3%/yr) plus modest load-factor and yield recovery; cross-checked against the through-COVID FY2019-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 2.8% and the 2.8% FY2019-25 figure rather than the COVID-base 3yr/5yr CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr and 5yr revenue CAGRs (27.9%, 14.5%) are COVID-trough artefacts (FY2022 revenue 87bn, FY2020 93bn) and are not growth rates. Attributable equity CAGR is negative (-12.5% 5yr, -4.6% 3yr) because FY2020-22 losses of 55.7bn consumed book value; EPS was negative FY2020-FY2024 so EPS CAGRs are undefined. Owner FCF (lease-adjusted) has been negative or near zero in every year except FY2023, so FCF CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Pre-COVID anchor FY2019: revenue 154,322, EBITDA 35,458 (23.0%), attributable NI 2,640. FY2025: revenue 182,256, EBITDA 40,792 (22.4%), attributable NI 855. Volume has recovered past 2019 (174m passengers, 972 aircraft vs ~860) but profit has not, because yield/RPK fell to 0.46 and interest plus lease costs on a larger fleet absorb the operating result.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation. FY2026 is a fuel-shock trough (H1 operating loss 1,799) and an investment year (net cash capex ~29bn, commitments 172.7bn), after which the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin returns to the 21.5% band the airline earned in FY2019 and FY2023-25. Revenue grows with the fleet plan (988 -> 1,104 aircraft by 2028) at 5-7% then decays to 3%. Lease cost drifts from 12.5% to 11.5% of revenue, cash capex settles at 9%, cash tax at 25%. The flows say what the history says: EBITDA of ~21% is fully consumed by lease rentals (~12%), owned-fleet reinvestment (~9%) and tax, leaving an owner-FCF margin under 1% at maturity against 142bn of net borrowings and 21bn of NCI. Equity value is negative; the H-share price rests on state support and recovery optionality, not on discounted cash flow.
scenario_narratives.bull: Yield recovery plus fuel relief plus cheaper fleet. EBITDA margin climbs to 25% (above any historical year), lease cost falls to 10.5%, capex to 8.5%; growth 9% fading to 3%. Owner-FCF margin reaches ~4% by year 10. Even this leaves enterprise value short of net borrowings plus NCI: the equity needs an EV roughly double the bull-case DCF to justify the current H-share price.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural yield decline continues under fleet growth and high-speed rail competition, fuel stays elevated, subsidies shrink. EBITDA margin 19%, lease cost flat at 12.5%, capex 9.5%. Ex-lease EBIT never turns positive, FCF is negative every year, the terminal value is floored at zero, and equity is wiped on a going-concern basis absent recapitalisation.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A lease-adjusted, mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on consolidated flows in RMB, discounted at a CNY WACC and converted to HKD at the quote. Leases are treated as an operating cost (treatment B) so lease liabilities stay out of net debt; NCI is deducted once at book; associates/JVs and non-cash financial assets are added at book. The model deliberately does not credit state support, A/H arbitrage or recovery optionality: it answers only what the discounted cash flows to the H-share are worth, and that answer is below zero in every scenario because the enterprise is almost entirely owned by lenders and lessors.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin, not discount rate, drives the result: each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is ~2-3bn RMB/yr of FCF, more than the entire base-case terminal-year FCF.

Lease treatment (B) charges finance-lease principal (19.8bn) above ROU amortisation (17.9bn); if the purchase-option fleet is thought of as owned, ~2bn/yr of the charge is equity build-up in aircraft rather than cost. This is worth ~RMB 1/share over the horizon and does not change the sign.
NCI deducted at book (21.2bn) although the subsidiaries earn ~68% of group profit; an earnings-based NCI claim would be larger and the H-share value lower.

Net cash capex is taken as reported; if sale-and-leaseback refunds of pre-delivery payments are netted inside the capex line, the FY2026 capex assumption of 15% may be high by a few points, which moves year-1 FCF by ~5bn but not the terminal.

Refinancing: 92.9bn of borrowings are current (ultra-short-term bills and bank loans at 1.2-2.9%); the valuation assumes they roll at policy rates. A move to commercial rates adds ~1.5-3bn/yr of interest, which is outside the unlevered flows but inside the equity's survivability.
State action in either direction: a parent recapitalisation (as in 2020) dilutes; a policy-driven fuel surcharge or route subsidy expansion lifts margins; neither is modelled.

FX: RMB-denominated value translated at CNY/HKD 1.1722 (2026-10-11); a 5% RMB move shifts the HKD IV by the same proportion. Most lease liabilities are USD/EUR, so a weaker RMB also raises lease cost and finance charges.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 2.815-6.62. FX from Yahoo CNYHKD=X; A-share reference from Yahoo 600029.SS.
data_sources.financials: 1055.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, RMB millions, IFRS); FY2025 annual report (operating expense table lines 1230-1254, note 12 D&A, note 21 right-of-use assets, consolidated cash flow statement lines 5904-5950, fleet plan lines 1895-1922, commitments line 1409); H1 2026 interim report (operating expenses lines 866-900, balance sheet lines 2452-2531, cash flow lines 2607-2650, fleet table lines 746-776, commitments line 381); kpis table for lease principal, lease liabilities, cash taxes, interest income, NCI dividends.
data_sources.qualitative: No Analysis JSON exists for this ticker; bull/bear axes drawn from the FY2025 and H1 2026 management discussion (fuel, yield/RPK, fleet plan, subsidies, high-speed rail risk section) and the capital commitments notes.

inputs.share_count_basis: 18,121m A+H shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report, share capital RMB18,121m at RMB1 par; weighted average 18,121m FY2024 and FY2025). No options, convertibles or SBC; held flat. The 2020 H-share placement was the last issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme disclosed in the FY2025 annual report or H1 2026 interim report (SOE; staff costs note 13 lists salaries, retirement scheme and termination benefits only). SBC = 0 by disclosure, not by omission.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 lease-adjusted owner FCF: reported FCF 14,944 (OCF 32,711 - capex 17,767) less capital element of lease rentals 19,778 = -4,834 (levered, after all interest paid). Unlevered equivalent, adding back borrowing interest 2,911 (interest paid 5,811 less lease interest 2,900) and stripping interest received 313: -2,236. FY2024 on the same basis: -7,998; FY2023: +2,494. The business has not produced positive unlevered owner FCF in a normal year; fleet growth has been debt-funded (borrowings 51bn FY2019 -> 150bn H1 2026).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income (338 FY2025) sits in finance income below operating profit and so is already outside the EBITDA the component build starts from; net borrowings of 142bn make the net-cash double-count rule moot. Set to 0.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX H-share quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1722 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-11T14:21Z. All per-share values computed in RMB then multiplied by 1.1722. No same-class dual listing exists for a parity tie: the A-share (600029.SS, RMB 4.85 at the 2026-10-09 Shanghai close) converts to HK$5.69 at this rate, so the H-share trades at a ~50% discount to the A-share, a structural A/H gap rather than an FX direction error. Direction check: HK$2.865 / 1.1722 = RMB 2.44 per H share against attributable book value of RMB 1.67 per share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity 9.6% = 10y CGB 1.8% + 1.3 beta x 6.0% China ERP. Cost of debt: FY2025 interest paid 5,811 on ~236bn average borrowings plus leases = 2.5% blended; stated borrowing rates 1.20-2.91% (interim note 17); after 25% tax 1.9%. Market weights (H-share equity 44bn + NCI 21bn vs net borrowings 142bn) give E/V ~31% and a mechanical WACC of ~4.2%; at A-share-implied equity ~5.1%. 5.5% applied: the only premium over the mechanical figure is ~0.5-1pp for the fact that 93bn of borrowings are current and are rolled at state-bank policy rates (ultra-short-term bills, 1.2-2.9%), which is a funding privilege rather than a market price of risk. No scenario-specific WACC and no further premium: cyclicality, fuel and yield risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash payment (capital element of lease rentals 19,778 in financing + interest on lease liabilities 2,900 in operating, FY2025; 12.4% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (104,293 at 30 June 2026: 19,699 current + 84,594 non-current) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only (92,915 current + 57,554 non-current). D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use amortisation: FY2025 D&A 31,209 less ROU amortisation 17,916 (note 21) = 13,293, 7.3% of revenue. Short-term lease expense (1,904) is already in operating expenses and so already inside the EBITDA margin. Treatment (A) was tested and is harsher (full D&A 17.1%, ROU additions 7.5% of revenue as capex-like, plus 104bn in the bridge); (B) is preferred because 61 of 78 FY2025 deliveries were finance leases with purchase options whose principal repayments buy the aircraft outright (9,327 transferred to PP&E on option exercise in FY2025), so the cash lease line is the economic fleet cost.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (EBITDA includes Xiamen Airlines, Chongqing, Henan, Guizhou and other majority-owned subsidiaries); non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book value, 21,153 at 30 June 2026. Note this is lenient to H-shareholders: NCI took 1,828 of FY2025 group profit (68%) against 41% of group equity, because the subsidiaries are more profitable than the parent. Net income in the Metrics CSV is attributable-only and is not used by the component build.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (CNY WACC, HKD quote with FX bridge, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero market). Routed as an operating company (airline) per the dcf-methods table; not a bank/REIT/LIC. CYCLE: FY2020-22 were COVID losses (-10.8bn, -12.1bn, -32.7bn attributable) and are not used as a base; FY2025 (EBITDA margin 22.4%, attributable NI 855) is near mid-cycle on volume but on depressed yields (yield/RPK -4.2% to RMB0.46); H1 2026 (EBITDA margin 15.1%, operating loss 1,799, attributable loss 3,699) is a fuel-shock half (flight operation expenses +25% on 'high and volatile oil prices'), treated as a year-1 trough, not a trend. Mid-cycle post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin anchored at 21.5% (FY2019 23.0%, FY2023 20.5%, FY2024 21.0%, FY2025 22.4%; shaded for structural yield pressure from high-speed rail and 13% planned fleet growth 2025-28). EBITDA includes 'other net income' (route subsidies / aircraft operation compensation, 4,292 FY2025, 5,909 FY2024), a recurring feature of Chinese airline P&Ls, consistently through the history. CAPEX: FY2026 is an investment year (H1 2026 cash capex 20,599 vs 5,876 pcp; construction in progress 30.4bn; capital commitments 172.7bn at 30 June 2026 after the 137-aircraft A320neo order of 29 Apr 2026 and the B777F order of 26 Jun 2026); fleet plan 972 -> 988 (2026) -> 1,054 (2027) -> 1,104 (2028). Most deliveries are finance-leased (61 of 78 in FY2025), so they arrive through the lease line rather than cash capex. BALANCE SHEET: net current liabilities 118bn; borrowings rose 16bn in H1 2026 to fund the loss and capex. No dividend to shareholders since FY2019. FINDING: on cash-flow fundamentals the H-share equity is a thin, highly levered sliver of a ~250bn RMB enterprise (net borrowings 142bn + leases 104bn against post-IFRS-16 EBITDA 40.8bn, 6.0x); every scenario including the bull returns a negative equity value, and the market price (1.46x attributable book on the H line, 2.9x on the A line) is paying for state support, refinancing certainty and recovery optionality that a going-concern DCF does not credit. The sensitivity that matters is EBITDA margin, not WACC: each 1pp of mid-cycle margin is ~1.8-2.8bn RMB/yr of FCF. SCREEN NOTE: this ticker would have been deferred by the queue rules (ND/EBITDA > 5x, interest cover < 2x on EBIT ex-lease vs total interest).

bear.narrative: Fuel stays high; 13% fleet growth to 2028 lands in a domestic market where high-speed rail caps yields and the Big Three keep adding capacity, so yield/RPK keeps sliding; subsidy income continues to shrink (other net income 5.9bn -> 4.3bn FY2024-25). EBITDA margin settles at 19%, below the FY2023 trough-recovery year. Ex-lease EBIT is negative in perpetuity, terminal value hits the zero floor, and the equity has no going-concern cash-flow value: survival depends on state-bank refinancing of 93bn of current borrowings and, eventually, a recapitalisation that dilutes H-shareholders.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.5%: H1 2026 revenue +9.7%, H2 assumed +6% on a strong FY2025 H2 base. Then fleet-plan growth (4-7%/yr deliveries net of disposals 2026-28) with flat-to-slightly-recovering yields, decaying to 3% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 17.5%: H1 actual 15.1% plus a seasonally stronger H2 at ~20% with fuel still elevated. Recovery to the 21.5% mid-cycle by FY2030 as fuel normalises and the 2025 yield decline (-4.2%) stabilises; no yield recovery to 2019 levels assumed.
base.lease_rationale: 12.5% = H1 2026 actual (10,408 principal + 1,411 interest on 94,679 revenue). Drifts to 11.5% as finance leases with purchase options roll into owned aircraft (FY2023 16.7% -> FY2025 12.4%), partly offset by finance-leased A320neo/C919 deliveries.
base.da_rationale: D&A ex-ROU 7.3% FY2025, 6.6% FY2024; rises to 7.8% as the owned fleet share grows (PP&E 119bn + CIP 30bn at H1 2026).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 15%: H1 cash capex 20,599 less 2,725 disposal proceeds = 17.9bn net in one half; H2 assumed lighter as PDPs convert to finance leases. 13% and 11% through the 87- and 76-aircraft delivery years, then 9% (FY2023-25 average 8.7%; 2018-19 average 13.4%) which is 1.15x D&A ex-ROU for 3% growth.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 30% of ex-lease EBIT near term (FY2025 paid 1,759 on EBIT ex-lease 4,821 = 36%, because profitable subsidiaries pay 25% while parent losses give no group relief), easing to the 25% statutory rate as the parent's 12.2bn deferred tax asset shelters parent profit. The engine charges no tax on a negative EBIT year, which under-states the subsidiary leakage in FY2026 by ~1.5bn; the later-year 30% over-charge roughly offsets.
base.wc_rationale: Negative working capital (sales in advance 9.2bn, accrued expenses 23bn) is roughly stable as a share of revenue; FY2025 cash generated from operations 39,968 vs EBITDA 40,792 implies a WC drag of ~0.8bn. Capture set to 0.

bull.narrative: Fuel normalises in H2 2026; domestic capacity discipline among the Big Three lifts yield/RPK back toward RMB0.48-0.50; international long-haul (Guangzhou hub, Europe/Australia/SE Asia routes) restores premium mix; C919/A320neo deliveries cut unit cost; EBITDA margin reaches 25%, above any year in the history (FY2019 23.0%). Lease cost falls to 10.5% as purchase options are exercised. This still produces an FCF margin of only ~4% at maturity.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 35% from the 15% house default: net borrowings 142bn plus 104bn of leases on 40.8bn of EBITDA (6.0x), 118bn of net current liabilities, a live fuel shock (H1 2026 loss), five of the last six years loss-making at the attributable line, and a structural yield decline (-4.2% FY2025) into 13% planned fleet growth. Bull cut to 20% because it needs fuel relief, capacity discipline across three state-owned competitors and a yield recovery to coincide, and even then returns a negative equity value. Base 45%. Weights sum to 1.0.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
